utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, would you have the accused brought in, please? (Accused enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are the three interpretation booths prepared, ready? No problem? All right. Good morning. Does everybody hear me? Does the Prosecutor hear? Does the Defence hear? Mr. Blaskic, do you hear? GENERAL BLASKIC: Good morning. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume our hearing. We will sit this morning from 10.00 until 1.00 and since we will be working from 10.00 all of next week, except for Friday, this first period was a little bit disturbed as far as the schedule goes, but without any further ado, since everybody has identified himself and we know one another anyway, I therefore suggest that the Prosecutor take the floor and tell us which witness you intend to bring in now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This morning I intend to call Mr. Simon Leach. Your Honour, as Mr. Leach is being brought into the courtroom, I wish to inform the court that we intended to present an expert witness this morning, but because of scheduling problems he was not able to arrive today. He will be available here on Monday. If Mr. Leach has not concluded his testimony, which I do not anticipate he would, I would ask the indulgence of the court to break his testimony so the expert could be heard, and thereafter we could resume with Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I hope that the Defence has no objection to that. This is simply so that the trial can move forward quickly, unless you have any objection, but it does seem to me to be a good way to proceed, that when we have -- as a way of avoiding any difficulty in continuing the conduct of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We are pleased to accommodate the convenience of the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would also like to thank the other party for trying to work with the Presiding Judge and the two colleagues so that the trial can move forward without too many interruptions. Prosecutor, would you now please bring in your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour. (Witness enters court)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Simon Kenneth Martin Leach. Mr. Simon Leach (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please give a headset to the witness? . You may be seated but, Mr. Leach, we need to give you a headset so that you can understand. Mr. Simon Leach, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Leach, what is your present occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am currently a team leader in the investigator section in the office of the Prosecutor for the international Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Prior to coming to the Criminal Tribunal, what did you do for a living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a serving police officer in the British police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you please inform the court of your background, your education and your professional experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was educated through high school and left school at 16 years of age. I had a variety of positions before joining the British police in 1979. For a period of four years I was a uniformed officer carrying out general police duties both on mobile patrol and as a foot patrol officer. This was also interspersed with periods of attachments to certain investigative units. In 1984 I was appointed Detective Constable as an investigator. I served for two years as an investigator in the east Lancashire town of Accrington. Thereafter I moved to the drug squad, to investigate narcotics and drugs investigations. This involved investigations both locally, nationally and internationally. After two years with the Drugs Squad in 1988 I was promoted to Detective Sergeant, which gave me responsibility for investigative teams. Again, we would cover the general spectrum of criminal offences, crimes of dishonesty, crimes of violence, armed robbery, murder and the like. After three and a half years as a Detective Sergeant operating in a local station I then moved to a unit called the Crime Support Unit. This is a unit dedicated to the investigation of serious criminal offences. I worked with that unit for two and a half years. I investigated and was sent to various European countries on investigations, which included France, Spain, Germany, Italy and the British province of Gibraltar. I was subsequently promoted to inspector and I was then back into uniform and given responsibility for divisional area with a team of five to six sergeants and 30 constables with a variety of responsibilities for general policing of the area of several towns, including criminal matters. In 1994 I went to the Home Office after short listing for an interview for a post here in the Tribunal as a team leader. After interview at the Home Office I was subsequently selected to join the Tribunal and came to the Tribunal in October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, could you describe your duties and responsibilities since you have been here at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After arriving at the Tribunal, my main area of responsibility has been to co-ordinate the investigations in relation to events in Central Bosnia. That is done in conjunction with investigators, military analysts, analysts, researchers and legal officers, who give legal direction to the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As the team leader and as an investigator, Mr. Leach, have you travelled to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been to Central Bosnia on at least 15 to 20 occasions in the last two and a half to three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher please, your Honour, to pass this map to Mr. Dubuisson, I would ask that be marked exhibit number 26, your Honour. I have copies for the convenience of the court and counsel, which I will now pass out. That, your Honour, represents a smaller version of exhibit number 26. Mr. Leach, what is the source of exhibit number 26?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a map, the opstina map of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is produced by the Director General of Military Surveyor at the Ministry of Defence in the United Kingdom. I believe the source for the Director General is an organisation called the Vojno Geografska Institute, which I think is an institute from the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you use the term "opstina", what you do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now that shows a number of municipalities, does it not, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To your right there's a pointer. Could you please point out the area of Central Bosnia on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Central Bosnia that we have been investigating in the Tribunal is generally this area here. The central point would be the town of Zenica and the surrounding municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you point out to the court, Mr. Leach, the municipalities of Vitez, Busovaca and Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vitez municipality is here. You may see a blue "YJ" just next to the name of Vitez, just underneath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could we move the easel a little bit to the right so that the Defence doesn't have to go through gymnastics in order to see it, so that he can see it better and also that we can see it better on the screens. Yes, that's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that exhibit number 26 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If there is no objection from the Defence, we can have it admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to pass the following exhibit, which would be number 27, to Mr. Dubuisson. If that could be put on the ELMO. Mr. Leach, exhibit number 27 appears also to be a map of Bosnia and Herzegovina divided by opstina, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On Exhibit 27 there appears to be in the centre of Bosnia and Herzegovina an area marked in yellow; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you please explain what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area marked in yellow is the area that is known as the Central Bosnia operative zone. This is the military zone which fell under the command of General Blaskic pre-November of 1992. It consisted of 22 municipalities. Those were the municipalities of Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Jablanica, Konjic, Novi Travnik, Travnik, Zenica, Jajce, Vitez, Busovaca, Kresevo, Kiseljak, Jarice, Kakanj, Fojnica, Zepce, Teslan, Zavidovici, Maglaj, Teslic and two small suburbs of Sarajevo, which you will notice are circled separately, called Stup and Krazinica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have the usher please take the next exhibit, which I would ask be marked as Exhibit 28. Mr. Leach, do you recognise exhibit number 28?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you explain to the court what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In early November 1992 there was a reorganisation of the HVO, which meant that five municipalities which had previously come under the command of General Blaskic no longer fell under his area of operations. He lost command responsibility for the municipalities of Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Jablanica and Konjic. You will notice note on the overhead and the map you have in front of you, your Honours, that there is a shaded area for the municipality of Jajce. This municipality for all intents and purposes fell out of command and control of General Blaskic in late November 1992 after it was taken by the army of the Republika Srpska, the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you point out the municipality of Jajce on exhibit number 28, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Leach, did the area in yellow represent the amount of territory that was in General Blaskic's area of control or does it represent something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The questioning has changed from command to area of control, and I would pose a foundation objection to testimony by this witness about control unless there is any basis for him to offer an opinion as to what territory or terrain was under the control of General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. (Pause.) We have deliberated, because this is a question of principle, and the Tribunal has decided that the witness was expressing himself freely as a prosecution witness, and therefore, Mr. Hayman, you will be able to contest anything you wish when you cross-examine during your questioning, and in that way you will be able to direct him in a different way. You can contest this point, which I understand might be important. So the witness can now continue and express himself as he wishes, according to the questions asked by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, could you answer the question I just posed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The area you see excluding Jajce after November 1992 displays for you the area, if you will, of responsibility based on a geographical area, in turn based on the municipalities indicated. It is not a true reflection of the area of control, because there will have been areas particularly to the north in the municipalities of Teslic, Teslan, Maglaj and Zavidovici which will have been under the control of other armies and not the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Exhibits 27 and 28 be admitted into evidence. Then I would ask the usher to present the next Prosecutor's exhibit, which is a large map. My assistant can point it out to him. Additionally, your Honours, I have copies of this map that I can provide to the court and to counsel. I have copies as well, your Honour, and they are to my left. The smaller, lighter roll, is for the Defence and the heavier roll is for the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Objections that the judges get a heavier roll and you are getting a lighter one? No. That's good. Thank you so much. Is that marked Exhibit 19 now? Thank you. Mr. Leach, what is the source of this particular map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another map which was originally provided for sourced to the Vojna Geografska Institute. Thereafter it was reproduced by a military surveyor UK for the use of UNPROFOR, when they first started to operate in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I would like you to take us through a tour of this particular region using that map. First of all, Mr. Leach, does this map reflect areas in the Vitez, Busovaca and Kiseljak municipalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Vitez is indicated at this point (pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You are pointing for the record to the top part of the map. Let me just ask you one additional question. You mentioned UNPROFOR. What is UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNPROFOR was the United Nations Protection Forces which were sent into the region to assist in peace-keeping and the delivery of food aid throughout the areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina and areas of Croatia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now does that map also include portions of the Zenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You are pointing now to the city of Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, could you just take us through some of the salient locations in that map. If you do so slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already indicated to you the town of Vitez, which was the main town for the municipality of Vitez. The other two main areas which are subject of the indictment are the municipalities of Busovaca and Kiseljak. I will now show you the municipality and the town of Busovaca (pointing). Kiseljak is in a south-eastern direction towards the bottom portion of your map to the right (pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If you could just hold the pointer there for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, what is the witness pointing to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the town of Kiseljak, which is the centre --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Kiss ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kiseljak, which is the town and the municipality of Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will now show you a series of records that were used by UNPROFOR, by the warring parties in the region and were the main mobile communication links in this area. The main road from the south of -- from Herzegovina, which food aid would travel through to Central Bosnia would commence in the south, from the area of Megovic and Mostar, which is not indicated on this map, but the route is this way through the town of Prozor to the town of Gornji Vakuf. The road then went to a very treacherous mountain area, and at that point you reach the town of Novi Travnik, which is shown on your map as Pucarvo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you spell that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: P-U-C-A-R-V-O. From Novi Travnik you can go to the junction of the main highway between Travnik and Zenica. So I will now show you the main highway from Travnik to Zenica. As you can see, the main highway travels through the town of Vitez. The next location I would bring to your attention is what we refer to in the team as the Busovaca T-junction, which is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The Busovaca T-junction is what, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this junction if you turn right, if you were travelling from Vitez, you would then start to travel towards the town of Busovaca and then through down to the town of Kiseljak. It is one of the main roads, the main communication links for the whole region. I'll now show you the route from the Busovaca T-junction. I will stop the pointer at Busovaca and then follow down through the town of Kiseljak (pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You are holding the pointer now at the town of Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you follow that route one more time, Mr. Leach, please, with your pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll follow the route again from Vitez to the Busovaca T-junction, to Busovaca, to Kiseljak (pointing). This is Vitez, Busovaca T-junction, which may be marked on your maps with the word "Kaonik"; south to Busovaca and then south-east to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, while you are standing, in what direction is Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sarajevo, if the map were larger, would be in this area here (pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, on that particular map, Exhibit 29, there are a number of locations marked or highlighted in orange. Can you explain what those are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. These are locations of villages which were attacked during the conflict between the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'll start at the west or the left-hand side of the map and work to the right, to the easterly side of the map (pointing). That location is Veceriska. The next location is Gacice. You then have the town of Vitez itself. Following the main highway you have Santici. Above Santici on the map you have Behrici. If you follow further down the road an inch and a half you then have Ahmici and Nadioci, followed by the village of Loncari. At the location I referred to as the Busovaca T-junction you have the former JNA barracks called Kaonik. If I then go south-west to the Kiseljak municipality, starting at the north of Kiseljak, there is the village of Svinjarevo; just at the south, Perici; just to the south again, Gromiljak -- sorry -- Gomionica; to the south again Gromiljak; to the south again Polje Visnjica and then south-west, Visnjica. To the south of Visnjica is Rotilj and directly east is Kiseljak town itself. If you travel the road south towards Sarajevo, you have Han Ploca and Grahovci, and directly south finally Tulica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, those towns and villages that are marked in orange do not represent all of the towns and villages that were attacked by the HVO, do they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: May I ask about Sevreno in the Vitez area. Did you mention Sevreno? It's highlighted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, because that's not within the indictment, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, you have previously described the road. You have been on those roads many times, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now the roads between Vitez and Kiseljak, along that road there are a number of villages that are highlighted in orange. Are many of those villages visible from that main route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from the village of Tulica to the south and portions of Rotilj to the west of Kiseljak, and also Loncari and Putis, all other locations are either exactly on the roadside where the village starts to exist or they are just one or two kilometres from the roadside and are quite clearly visible to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would move into evidence exhibit number 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May I be heard, your Honour? My only concern is if there are some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, we are listening to you. I'm not sure we can hear you but we're listening. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: My only concern is if there is some confusion about which villages are mentioned in the indictment and have been highlighted, that that be clarified before the map be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What confusion, Mr. Hayman? Could you be a little clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Well, Judge Shahabuddeen enquired about the village of Sevreno, which is apparently highlighted in orange, but which is not named in the indictment. I just think for clarity it would be good to be consistent. I think there was testimony the highlighted villages were the ones named in the indictment. Now apparently that's not the case with respect to at least one. If that could be clarified, I think that would be helpful to all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is sustained. Therefore if the exhibit is going to be admitted, it should be first corrected and only then admitted. Therefore, I propose that for the moment this exhibit will be returned to the Registry and will be resubmitted later, when the Tribunal will admit it once it has been corrected. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Leach, that's a very large map next to you, but the area that's depicted in that map, is it a very large area in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, from the town of Vitez to Kiseljak, when you were travelling by road, not as the crow flies just by road, is less than 50 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two clear plastic overlays for that particular map, and I would ask that they be identified as Exhibit 29A and 29B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Under the same reservation, Mr. Prosecutor, the objection that was sustained. We will see what this overlay will show.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would ask that Mr. Leach assist the usher in mounting those on the exhibit. Your Honour, for the assistance of the court and counsel I now have something else that I would like to present to the court, and it is essentially a copy of the map as it now appears with those concentric circles over each location.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would you like them to be numbered separately as exhibits number 30 and 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Or they could be marked 29C and D.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is the question of numbers clear so that during the cross-examination we all understand what we are talking about regarding the exhibits? 29C will be the one referring to the zone to the south, the zone of Vitez. The area of Vitez will be 29C and the area of Kiseljak will then be 29D. Are we in agreement? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, why do not we start with 29C? First of all, Mr. Leach, can you explain what this is, 29C?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. 29C is the plastic overlay on the large map. The centre point for the overlap is in the town of Vitez and is as accurately as possible placed on the Hotel Vitez, which was the headquarters of General Blaskic during the period of the indictment. The rings then each depict a distance of 1 km as you leave the centre point of the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were distances taken by the office of the Prosecutor to various locations in respect of this investigation, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A large number of distances have been travelled by investigators in my team. This has been done by car, using the Hotel Vitez as the centre point and then travelling on the most accessible route, either main road or side road, to certain village locations on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, will you just for the court's benefit describe the various locations that are indicated on Exhibit 29C? That is the distances between the Hotel Vitez and the locations that you will testify about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first distance is from the Hotel Vitez to the village of Ahmici (pointing).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You are talking via the main road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is via the main road from Vitez to the main highway between Travnik and Zenica. That's a distance of 4.8 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next location is the village of Gacice to the west of Vitez. That is a distance of 1.9 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will you point that out on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing). The next location is the village of Veceriska, which is a distance of 3.9 kms (pointing).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting counsel and the witness but the witness is reading from some kind of a document. He has a blue bound folder. The problem with witnesses taking documents up to the witness stand and utilising them in their testimony in secret is it's a form of secret communication between the Prosecutor and the witness, if, in fact, the Prosecutor has the document or has seen it. I object to witnesses taking documents up to the witness stand without having them known to court and to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman. You know that in the first week we are going to deal with many problems of principle, and we hope to make progress in a positive sense. I must say that as far as I am concerned, it seems to me to be rather difficult to ask a witness to come with his hands in his pockets and to answer such complex questions. You know that after all if he knew all that by heart, it would boil down to the same thing. So I do not think it is a fundamental objection. If a witness has a document he is like any other person. His memory may fail him, and so he needs some documents. If those documents are tele-guided by the Prosecutor, I think that's very difficult to answer that question. You can't answer it and I can't either. Nonetheless I will ask my colleagues and consult them, but I would appeal to you to allow the witnesses to express themselves and to have some confidence in them, and after that you can question them as much as you wish, but allow me to consult my colleagues first, because during this week we need to regulate certain matters regarding the conduct of the debates at this hearing. (Pause.) We are trying to adjust to different judicial cultures. The Tribunal has tried to make a distinction between what are personal notes -- every individual has his way of preparing himself for a hearing -- and, on the other hand, documents which have to be common to all, and which the Prosecutor has knowledge of. If this document that Mr. Leach has on his table -- if it is a document known to the Prosecution, then the Tribunal feels it agrees with the Defence and it should be conveyed to the Defence. If these are personal notes and the witness will tell us under oath they are personal notes intended to help him personally during his testimony, which, as we see, will last for several hours, if they are personal notes, then the Tribunal feels that they belong to Mr. Simon Leach and he may use them. Therefore, my question is, Mr. Simon Leach, whether the document identified by the Defence as being on your table, is it a document that the Prosecutor is familiar with? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is a document that you drew up with the Prosecutor or at least that the Prosecutor was aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Prosecutor is aware of it. It is an aide memoire so I am aware of what exhibits will come in what order. Interspersed into that are my own personal notes so that I can then refresh my memory on factual things such as distances, the names of municipalities, etc. It's an aide memoire for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now this is a different situation. It is a document established with the Prosecutor as well as being an aide memoire at the same time. (Pause.) In accordance with our position, this document will be communicated to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Now, Mr. Leach, will you please continue with your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. (Pause.) Very well. The document will be communicated to the Defence, but it will not be admitted as evidence for the Tribunal. You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, we were discussing Exhibit 29C. Could you continue, please, and advise the Trial Chamber and counsel the distances in relation to various locations on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. I'd previously pointed out the village of Ahmici at 4.8 kms and the village of Gacice at 1.9 kms. The next location is Visnjica at 3.9 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again travelling from Hotel Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, again travelling from the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next location is the village of Santici, which is 4.4 kms from the Hotel Vitez. The next location is the village of Behrici, which is 5 kms from the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Behrici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Behrici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the map, sir, it's just north, about 1 and a half cms, from Santici. The next location is the village of Nadioci, which is to the east of Ahmici, and 6 kms from the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next location is the Busovaca T-junction, which I must apologise to the court. I do not have my notes with me for this, but I can show the location. (Pointing). You can see from the concentric rings that it is approximately 9 kms from the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Shall we now turn to Exhibit 29D, Mr. Leach, and could you please repeat the exercise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. (Pause.) You may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. If I may correct my previous answer, I do have a supporting aide-memoire with me, which obviously the Defence will get. The distance from the Hotel Vitez to Kaonik Prison is 10.6 kms. Obviously the difference on the concentric circles is because the concentric circles is a direct route as the crow flies. The 10.6 kms is as you would travel by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we now turn to Exhibit 29D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the same methodology which is applied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. This simply means, Mr. Harmon, that the map which was prepared very carefully does not allow us to use it -- does not allow us to use the scale indicated on the map, because the distance are calculated differently on the ground. I'm sorry. Perhaps it would have been simpler to have said how many kms Kaonik was away from such and such a point because here you have concentric circles but if you calculate in west to east you do not come up with the same differences. You yourself had to correct yourself, Mr. Simon Leach. I am not reproaching you for anything. You paid a lot of attention in doing it. I want to make the proper estimates because I was very carefully trying to make calculations of the kilometres and it did not match. Therefore I think the simplest thing to do or say is to say, as in all countries, that Kaonik has to be so many kilometres from the other place using the most direct route. I'm just making a simple comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Mr. Leach, would you turn to 29D now, which is the southern most set of concentric circles. Would you please first of all indicate what is the centre point in 29D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The centre point for Exhibit 29D is the former JNA barracks which was the Kiseljak barracks, which was under the control of the HVO and also a headquarters of General Blaskic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the distances in that particular exhibit, is that also 1 km distances between the concentric rings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Leach, would you please now describe to the court the distances by car between certain locations indicated in orange on 29D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. The distance from the Kiseljak barracks to Svinjarevo is 7.3 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Svinjarevo is the mark that's located at the top of the exhibit, around 6 km mark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The next location is that of Behrici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: To go back to what I was saying, all of this may be cross-examined. Just tell us simply that these concentric circles allow you to make specific estimates, at least more or less specific. Simply tell us how far are these -- what are the distances of these points marked in orange on the map? Those to the east are further away than what is shown in your concentric circles. So I think we go a little bit more quickly to explain this. Tell us very quickly how far away about Kiseljak was from the 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 or 9 locations which I have indicated on the map. I think that would be easier and then we can ask questions that are asked so as to speed things up a bit. (Pause.) Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The concentric circles are not to confuse the Chamber as to the distances travelled by car, but as the Chamber will hear later on, parts of the geography of this area is flat. So those concentric circles represent the distances by sight to those particular locations. That's the relevance of the circles, but they are not to be confused with the distances travelled by road. I'm very happy to proceed to have Mr. Leach continue by giving you the distance by road to these particular locations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll start again, your Honour -- should I -- from Kiseljak Barracks to Svinjarevo is 7.3 kms; the barracks to Behrici is 6.5 kms; the barracks to Gomionica is 6.6 kms; to Gromiljak is 3.3 kms; to Rotilj is 4.6 kms; Polje Visnjica, 4.2 kms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Visnjica 5.2 kms. Ploca 8.8 kms. I do not have a reading for Tulica. The reason for that is on a visit to that area we have been informed by both IFOR and SFOR that there's a possibility of mines and therefore it is not safe to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What's IFOR and SFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are the current stabilising forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Some of these places had barracks and some did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The centre point for the second exhibit, your Honour, this exhibit (pointing), there's only one barracks indicated on that exhibit. That is the Kiseljak Barracks, which was under the control of the HVO, and that was a former JNA barracks before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That was the only location which had barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Exhibit 29D be admitted into evidence. 29D does not have the offensive orange marked on a village that was not attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I would just like to comment on a point of visibility. Is it flat completely? Is the area flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two exhibits do differ substantially, your Honour. In the case of Kiseljak and the Kiseljak Barracks, it is highly unlikely, if impossible, to see the locations marked as a town, although during a conflict when, for example, smoke may be rising, you may be able to see the smoke, but line of sight to the hill where the village is situated I would say not. Alternatively, if you return to the previous exhibit for Vitez, on my personal visits you can stand in the town of Vitez. You can quite clearly see Gacice, Veceriska, Santici and Behrici from the town of Vitez itself. Those villages and locations are quite clearly identifiable. Therefore the concentric rings are even more valuable for you there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we're going to suspend the hearing and we will resume at 11.30. (11.15 am) (Short break) (11.40am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume the hearing. I would like to have the accused brought in, please. (Accused enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. If I could have the usher please take Exhibit 30. I would ask that to be marked as Exhibit 30 by Mr. Dubuisson. I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, before you use Exhibit 30, can you explain to the court the source of the map of the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a general autoroute map produced by the Shell Company. It is a scale of 1:250,000.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There seems to be an overlay on that map. Would you indicate what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the overlays which are equivalent in size to the first exhibit, the first opstina, municipality map that you were shown at the very beginning of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, is that an overlay of the Central Bosnia operation zone after 1972, November -- 1992, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's an outline and then the individual municipalities within the Central Bosnia operational zone post-November-1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is indicated in orange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The orange indicates where the municipalities of Vitez, Busovaca and Kiseljak would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now could you please remove the overlay with the orange from Exhibit 30? Now, your Honour, I have a smaller version of what is depicted in part of that map, and I would ask that that be distributed to counsel and to the court. Would you put that on the ELMO, please, Mr. Leach? Mr. Leach, could you orient the court as to particular features on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. To the bottom left-hand corner of the map you see the city of Den Haag, where we are now. That is a representation within there. Going up the map is the municipality of Kiseljak, which goes as far as Leiden. You then have what would be the municipality of Busovaca, where you can see the town of Nieuw-Vennep, followed by the municipality of Vitez, which would end just before the city of Amsterdam, but would go as far as Schipol Airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that Exhibit 30 and 30A be admitted to evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No objection to Exhibit 30, your Honour, if there's a foundation that the two maps are of the same scale. I do not think we have heard that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware they are of the same scale. The opstina map that was used to draw the overlay is of the same scale but I'll check my notes. (Pause) I understand they are of the same scale but I cannot be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with that answer, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the court could enquire what map, if it's an exhibit, the overlay of the Bosnian area came from and then that might help. It is not clear in my mind that they are the same scale. They may well be but I just do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand it's come from the Bosnian opstina map but I didn't prepare the overlay myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can present evidence to the court on that later, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, do you want to -- I didn't quite understand your answer. Would you like to clarify it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not have the specific map and I can't reference the specific map today, your Honour, or this morning. I can at a later hearing. They are from maps of the same scale, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For the time being we will see that map 30 does not cause you any problems for its being put into the record. Which one are you asking questions about? 30A,; Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I think 30 is the map before the witness. If I understand the witness' testimony properly, the question is: is Exhibit 28 also of the scale of 1:250,000? It may indicate on the copy that was tendered to the Registrar. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, I do not have that information at my fingertips. I can present that information to the court at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. The Tribunal will wait to have the exhibits put into the record until we have clarified the point. In the meantime, let us continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just assist the court, if Mr. Hayman refers to the notes, -- the copy of my notes, page 1, the Bosnia-Herzegovina opstina map says "Scale 1:500,000". If you refer to the map of Holland Shell, page 6, the scale is 1:500,000 so they are the same scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That's fine, though the witnessed testified that the map of Holland was 1:250,000, so that was perhaps the source of my confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, for the time being we will take note of your confusion. You can save your objections until you cross-examine. In the time being the Tribunal will agree to postponing of the exhibit being put into the record until next week, when the Prosecutor brings us clarifications. If the clarifications are insufficient you can draw whatever conclusions you choose to during your cross-examination. Now I would like to give the floor back to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like this following exhibit marked Exhibit 31. Mr. Leach, what is exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. I have been asked a question by the Registrar. Could you -- we'd like to know whether this overlay has been recorded as 30B -- D -- I'm sorry. 30D. I'm talking now about the overlay. I believe that it is part of -- an integral part of 30, which for the time being has not been admitted as an exhibit. Yes. Is this an integral part of 30A, Mr. Dubuisson, in which case it would also not be put in as evidence until you -- or do you consider it should be put in as an exhibit? Mr. Hayman, what do you think? Would you prefer that it be part of that other exhibit until we come to our definite conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would think it should be 30A or 30B. I would guess 30A since there is only one other map an overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You have no problem with its being put in as an exhibit then?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Until we know its scale, I would suggest that it stay together with Exhibit 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I agree that's more logical. For 30A -- turning to the Registrar, come help me for a moment. These are pieces for the time being -- the pieces we are not putting in are 30A-D, is that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, the parts put in abeyance is the map on the easel, which is map 30. The little map which is attached is 30A, which is being postponed -- being put into the record is being postponed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Since there is the problem of scale with all three documents for the time being we will hold all three in abeyance. You can continue with the map you have there, Mr. Leach, in order to answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have reproductions of this as well, your Honour, for the court and counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If we all agree, as far as the numbering is concerned, the large map will be 31 and the one which has been tendered to the judges will be 31A, that's the smaller one. Do we agree to that before we know whether we are going to bring them in as evidence? Everybody does agree. All right. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, what is the source of 31?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The source of this map is the Cartographic Institute in Den Haag, which is indicated actually on the map, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you explain this exhibit, please, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The concentric circles that you can see on the map are representative of a distance of 1 km between each circle. Indicated on the map are a variety of locations by letter, letter A being the Hotel Vitez; letter B thereafter being the village of Ahmici; C, the village of Santici; D, the village of Gacice; E, the village of Sivrino Selo; F, the village of Donje Veceriska. G is what we would call the front line entry point in Stari Vitez. H is the site of a truck bomb explosion which occurred in the afternoon of 18th April 1993 in Stari Vitez. I is what is described as an exit point from Stari Vitez. J is the village of Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the map of The Hague what is the centre point A represented by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The centre point on the actual map is Central Station, but we refer to this -- we can refer to this as the Hotel Vitez for comparison of distances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So A is overlaid over the Central Station, train station in The Hague; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then the distances to the various other letters are indicated in the legend which is located in the upper right-hand corner of this map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So Ahmici, where in The Hague would Ahmici appear, Mr. Leach, from the Central Station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the Central Station Ahmici would appear at point B, which is the pier at Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you point that out, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing). That is Central Station or would be General Blaskic's headquarters in Vitez. That is the peer at Scheveningen (pointing) or would the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Referring to letter C, which is the village of Santici, where in The Hague approximately does the letter C show up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letter C shows up at the harbour to the east -- the north side of the harbour at Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, turning to Gacice, which is indicated by letter D, where on the map of The Hague does the letter D appear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter D is just at the car park and the junction of the Peace Palace.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Turning to the letter F, which is Donje Veceriska, where on this map does the letter F appear in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appears on Zwolsestraat, where it joins Van Alkemade- laan, but it is best described being 150-200 metres beyond the prison at Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now could you turn to the letter G, Mr. Leach, and tell me where in The Hague the letter G appears and what is the location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: G is near to the park and the museum not far from the American Embassy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How far away is that from the Central Station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's 1.9 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. It's 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now the letter G that you've just referred to, what did you refer to in the town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you were at point A, which would be the Hotel Vitez, as the fighting between the two warring parties commenced on 16th April in Vitez town, a front line, if you will, developed between the two warring parties, and that front line would be indicated at point G.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What does point H represent in the town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Point H represents an incident which occurred on the afternoon of 18th April 1993, where a large truck or van loaded with a substantial amount of explosives exploded inside what had then developed into the Muslim enclave, and this bomb exploded in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Referring to the map of The Hague, where does that appear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That appears to the left side of the Malieveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, turning to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Would you explain where Malieveld is for the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you leave Central Station, your Honour, and I drive towards the beach, there's a very large park on your right, which is often the site for circuses and fairs. The central part of that park or the central entrance to that park would be the Malieveld.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How many metres would that be from the Central Station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's about 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Turning lastly, Mr. Leach, to the letter J, what does that represent in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That represents the village of Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where on the map of The Hague does it appear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That appears out towards Wassenaar, in between The Hague and Wassenaar on the main highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Exhibits 31 and 31A be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The exhibits have been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would ask that the following exhibit be marked as Exhibit 32. Mr. Leach, I would like to turn to Exhibit 32. Can you first of all identify the source of that particular map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This map has been provided under the auspices of the Director General of the Military Surveyor, Ministry of Defence, United Kingdom, dated May 1993. It's printed by the Military Survey of UK.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will you please explain to the court what Exhibit 31 represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a town plan of Vitez. I should point out to your Honours that not every single building, not every complete black square or rectangle is representative of every building in the town, but it does give a fairly accurate assessment of the buildings in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance between the concentric rings on that town -- on that map, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The concentric rings indicate a distance of 200 metres from one ring to the next.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the centre point of the first circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The centre point is the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could, Mr. Leach, would you please proceed to describe to the court the first location on that map, which would be indicated as letter B, first of all pointing it out to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Hotel Vitez would be here at A, your Honours, and B is the Vitez Cinema.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the Vitez Cinema? Can you explain what it is first of all, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it is a combination of a cinema building and cultural centre that was for the residents of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if I may have these photographs as my next exhibit, your Honour, exhibit number 33, there are 11 photographs in each of the files. Now, Mr. Leach, let me ask you a question in respect of those particular photographs. Have you had a chance to inspect those photographs Exhibit 33?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell me when those photographs were taken and whether you were present at the time those photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These photographs were taken by two photographers from the Dutch National Police, who were requested to assist the office of the Prosecutor taking photographs of various locations throughout Central Bosnia. These particular photographs were taken on Tuesday, 28th May 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I would move to admit Exhibit 33, which is 11 photographs contained in the book I just passed to the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I think they should be identified first so that we know they are relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I was intending to do that, your Honour, as I was going to go through the rest of my examination. I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Prosecutor, for the moment we will give them numbers. What are the numbers, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is exhibit number 33. The first photograph will be 33-1 and so on until 33-... how many are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There are 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 33-12 my colleague tells me. Very well, Mr. Prosecutor. Will you identify them, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, will you identify the photographs in Exhibit 33, please, starting from the top, which is PH181?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: PH181, your Honours, is a photograph taken from the front but slightly to the left of the Hotel Vitez, which was the headquarters of General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now would I like to turn to PH186, Mr. Leach. Can you identify that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph taken directly from the road to the front entrance of the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which was General Blaskic's headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The interpreters are telling me that they would prefer to see the photographs on the ELMO, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are in the stage of identification now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you wish me to start again at the beginning, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I would prefer you to do that so as to facilitate our work. Go on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the first photograph that was shown, which was PH181, which is the front of the Hotel Vitez taken from the left side of the building. The next photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. I think the ELMO has to be adjusted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next photograph, PH186, is from the road looking directly at the entrance of the Hotel Vitez, which was General Blaskic's headquarters. The next photograph relevant to General Blaskic headquarters is PH205. This is taken from a pedestrianised walk area where no vehicles are allowed and is to the side of the hotel. One can see the hotel sign at the top of the building. The next photograph I will show you is PH182, which is at the front of your binder. PH182 is a photograph of the telecommunications building, the PTT, which was under the control of the local Bosnian Croats and HVO during the period of the conflict. The next photograph I will refer to I think is the fourth page, PH208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Indicate the number of the photograph, because they are not in the same order, as far as we can see here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is PH208.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which will be found on the last page, your Honour, of your ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a second photograph of the PTT building in Vitez. The next photograph I will show you is on page 2 and its number is PH197. This is a photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Wait a second. That should be on the fifth page of your books, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm managing to find my way as long as I'm given the number of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken from the rear of the Cinema building, the cultural centre, slightly off-set to the right, looking back at the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the significance of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the morning of 16th April 1993, when the conflict erupted, a large number of Bosnian Muslim civilians from various locations throughout the town of Vitez itself were taken to this building, where they were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next photograph, your Honour, is PH198. This is another photograph of the cinema building, but actually shows the entrance door to the building from the side. The next photograph is PH203.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you identify it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the front entrance of what was the headquarters of the local HVO brigade in Vitez, under the command of a man by the name of Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Could you proceed with the next photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next photograph, your Honour, is PH225.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a photograph taken of a building known as the Vetrinaska Stanista, which is the veterinary station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the significance of that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a separate location again used on the morning of 16th April 1993 where Bosnian Muslim civilians were taken and detained as the conflict started that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Could you proceed with the next photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next photograph, your Honour, is PH226 and this is another photograph of the same building from the previous picture, the veterinary station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Leach. Please proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The final picture is PH212.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is believed to be the location of the premises which are in the ground floor or basement known as the Chess Club.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the significance of the Chess Club?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the conflict on 16th April a large number of Bosnian Muslims were detained in a variety of locations. Over the following days negotiations took place --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid I have to object as to foundation. I do not know what the source of this witness' knowledge is for events that clearly he was not present for, if they occurred, because he had not yet become involved in the activities of the Tribunal. I have no objection to him identifying a location, as he was told this was the Chess Club or whatever, and perhaps other witnesses can provide details of events that occurred in the 1992, etc., time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I agree with you that the witness certainly did not participate in the events. Will you continue, Mr. Leach.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, your Honour, I would ask that the exhibit, the photo book marked as Exhibit 33, be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The album will be admitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Leach, if we could return, please, to the previous exhibit, which is the Vitez town plan, Exhibit 31, and you had previously identified the Vitez Cinema, both in the photographs and designated by the letter B on the exhibit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now can you please tell the court the distance from the Hotel Vitez, which was General Blaskic's headquarters, to the Vitez cinema?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximately 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And that appears on the map with a letter B; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I would like to turn your attention to the letter C on that map. First of all, can you tell me what the letter C represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letter C represents the location of the veterinary station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance of the veterinary station from General Blaskic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 900 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now turning to the letter D that appears on that exhibit, can you identify what that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Location of letter D is a building known as the Dubrovica School.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was the Dubrovica School to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again to my knowledge it was another location where not only people from Muslims -- Bosnian Muslims from the town of Vitez but also Bosnian Muslims from other locations in other villages were also detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance of the Dubrovica School from the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's 2.6 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now turning to the letter E on the map, what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letter E represents the Vitez Chess Club.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance of the Vitez Chess Club from General Blaskic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The distance is 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now turning to the letter F, what is the letter F on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letter F is the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance of the PTT building from General Blaskic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 75 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now turning to the letter G on that map, what does the letter G represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter G represents the location of where the front line developed between Muslim forces in Stari Vitez and the HVO units in Vitez town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On 16th April 19 96 -- 1993, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as it developed on 16th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance from General Blaskic's headquarters to the front line entry of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now turning to the letter H, Mr. Leach, what does the letter H represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letter H represents the opposite side of the Muslim enclave of Stari Vitez, which would be where the other side of the confrontation line developed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How far away was that from General Blaskic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is 1.2 kms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Turning now to the letter I on that map, can you identify what that represents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I have a small question. If I look at your circles, H is at 200 metres and, the fifth circle is 1200 and Dubrovica School is at 2,060 metres. So what is the difference? Was it 1,000 or 1200 metres roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference by the concentric circles again is the line of sight distance but if you get in a car and drive from the Hotel Vitez and follow the road, if I may show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that then becomes 2.6 kms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The letter I indicates the general location of where the truck bomb, which exploded on the afternoon of 18th April, took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now turning to the letter J, can you tell us what that represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The letter J relates to a local factory premises, which was converted by the British battalion of UNPROFOR into a location they called the Echelon Garage. This was a location where a sub-unit of mechanical engineers could repair their vehicles and for refuelling purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was the significance of that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the conflict developed from 16th April through to 19th and 20th April 1993 a large number of Bosnian Muslim civilians congregated on that building seeking shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now move this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I am now going to ask that there be displayed a video tape. It's tape number 10. Can you refer to your notes and inform the court what they will see on video tape number 10?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As part of the mission when photographs of certain locations were taken in May 1996 the IFOR forces provided a helicopter for the Tribunal investigators, for myself and one of the Dutch police photographers. During a two and a half hour flight we flew around various locations taking a video film to depict the areas in the towns and villages. The clipping you'll see at tape 10 will represent the area of Stari Vitez and then the frame during the video presentation will freeze and I will be able to indicate to you where the Hotel Vitez is situated, to give you some idea of the geographic and topography of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will it also show, Mr. Leach, the Cerkez's headquarters building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could have the lights dimmed, we could then proceed with tape 10. Mr. Leach, if you just narrate as we proceed through this tape. Can we have tape 10, please? (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the distance you will see the running track, which is indicated on the town plan, and here you have the site of the Vitez mass grave and the mosque in Stari Vitez. You can see the destruction of buildings in the foreground. We are now travelling down a road which leads towards the Hotel Vitez and the site of the truck bomb. The helicopter is almost over the Hotel Vitez a few seconds ago, and what you are seeing is in the main now the whole area of Stari Vitez. The area in the centre picture now indicates where the bodies from the deceased persons from the village of Ahmici were buried. We have almost completed a full circle in the air and you'll see some apartment buildings coming into view. Where that is stopped there's a white strip at the very top of the picture. That white strip is the top of the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the film clip 10 be admitted into evidence. (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There is more film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another close-up of Stari Vitez. We pass over the mosque and we are now just about to come over the area where the front lines developed just now, at that point, and you can see the apartment buildings in Vitez town proper. The building that has just come into view, and the frame should freeze, is the Hotel Vitez. There you have in the main centre picture the Hotel Vitez and in the bottom left-hand side of the picture is the PTT building. The Cerkez headquarters would just be out of sight at the top left corner of the picture. The helicopter now traversed around the town and here we have a view looking down through Vitez itself. The building to the top left of the picture is the Vitez school and shortly coming into the frame will be the back of the Cinema building that you have seen in the still photographs. That has just come into the frame now. Again in the frame here you can see, top right mid photograph is the Cerkez headquarters and the cinema complex and to the far left is the rear of the Hotel Vitez. So you can see the closeness of the two buildings. The building in the centre ground now is the municipal offices of Vitez, which again are opposite the Hotel Vitez and the PTT building. That was a general overview of the town of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, I'm going to ask you to describe two films that I'm now going to show to the Trial Chamber in respect of Ahmici. Will you please -- they are tapes 5 and tapes 6. First of all, can you explain to the court what they will see, but before you do that, would you explain when those films were taken and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The films were taken again on the same helicopter flight I described earlier, on Monday, 27th May 1996. I was present in the helicopter with a Dutch photographer who used the video camera. The two films you will see, the first one is taken from the air, which will give you a circumstance view or view on at least one occasion, and maybe two, of the village of Ahmici, and during that film I'll point out to you certain locations of the second video will thereafter show you in close-up video footage taken on the ground actually inside the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now if we could dim the lights, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Will these be marked as exhibits so the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I should think so, unless there are objections, but in theory I do not see why they would be -- wouldn't be put into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They have not yet been. They have been marked for identification as exhibits, so I would request that that be done and also request that the witness' description of the places depicted be limited to matters within his personal knowledge and that he not describe events to which he was not a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, we have already had this discussion. We had it yesterday. The Tribunal needs to be informed about everything and in complete detail. You will contest everything you like during the cross-examination and now you are contesting these films before even having seen them, but before we put into question the presence or the lack of presence of the witness' presence, everybody knows that this is a prosecution witness. You are contesting films which you have not even looked at. Please we will look at the films. Probably they will be part of the Prosecutor's evidence. We need to know all information, and you can contest what you like, but we do not have to go back to the conversation we had yesterday having to do with good conduct intended to move the trial forward properly, but please let's first take a look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have the lights dimmed, please, and then start with tape 5. Mr. Leach, if you would narrate the film. (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We now are over the village of Ahmici. The view you can see now is taken from the main highway, so if you were travelling down the main highway on the ground, that is what you would see. We've now turned left from the main highway. In the centre picture is a mosque with a minaret destroyed. In centre picture now is a grocery store and then the village road continues up the hillside. One can see the destroyed houses. Having travelled up the hillside to the top of the village, this is the far most point of the village. All the houses there are destroyed. The one with a roof has a roof intact but it's not habitable. We have now circled round the top of the village and are facing back down the Lasva Valley towards Vitez and Travnik. So the helicopter is now travelling back towards the main highway between Vitez and Busovaca.
