This is a similar shot depicting the damage in the village, travelling from the uppermost part of the village. We've now circled round. The building which has now come into view is called the upper mosque. There were two mosques, in the village of Ahmici. The one you saw briefly earlier had a minaret; this one did not have a minaret. This is approximately midway between the main road and the furthest most point of the village as you get to it at the top of the hill. The helicopter pilot has merely circled round so you get a view of all angles of that mosque. This is the lower mosque in Ahmici, the one with the minaret. This mosque is approximately 200 metres from the main highway and is quite clearly visible as you travel up and down the main highway, as is the majority of the destruction that you have seen in the village, apart from that in the upper part of the village at the very top. That gives you a view from behind the mosque and down the Ahmici road to the main highway. You can see vehicles traversing the main highway travelling from Vitez towards Zenica and Busovaca. That gives you a view back down through the valley to Vitez town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Leach, have you been to Vitez -- to Ahmici, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we could keep the lights dimmed, we'll turn to tape 6. Please explain what tape 6 is, Mr. Leach, as we go along. (Video tape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the video taken actually from the ground. It was done in a variety of means, either standing on foot and the photographer would simply traverse round to show you a picture of what was present. In order to give an indication and relate it to the aerial video, using a compass at this point the photographer held position and that is the general -- where he paused is the general direction of the city of Zenica. This video is taken right at the very top of the village. Busovaca would be over the hill that you see there and the town of Vitez would be behind the bushes that are now in the foreground. Halfway into the village of Ahmici there is a grocery store, which is still operating, and at this point we placed the camera man on the bonnet of a IFOR Landrover. He then sat on the Landrover and as we drove from the centre of the village to the top of the village, he then took video footage. Hence it's a little bit bumpy. We didn't have too much technical equipment to support us. The building that first came into view at that section was the upper mosque, and we are now travelling from the centre of the village towards the upper mosque and getting closer to it. Here you have a close-up on the ground picture of the upper mosque in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The distance from Ahmici to the Hotel Vitez where General Blaskic's headquarters were located was how far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's 4.8 kms. We've now reached the end of the passable roadway. It's possible to walk down on foot further. You can just see the tracks and some houses beyond, where there's a divergence in the fork. You then continue to the right. We're now approaching the very edge of the village at the highest point and that is as far as we could travel. You are able to travel a few hundred metres on foot but we were not allowed to travel because of the possibility of mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What are these buildings, Mr. Leach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the former buildings of residents from the village of Ahmici. We've now started again at the top of the village and have started to drive back down towards the centre. In effect we have just turned round. The reason to do this was just it was impossible to take an accurate video doing it in just one direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now are these destroyed Croat homes or destroyed Muslim homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware they are all Muslim homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When was the last time you were in Vitez -- sorry -- when was the last time you were in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are there any Muslims living in Ahmici today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no. That view you can see there is from the upper part of Ahmici. You would have a view down on to the village of Nadioci. The main Busovaca, Vitez, Zenica highway would go through the land that's in the far distance in the valley itself. Again that's the upper mosque in Ahmici. I should say, your Honours, that the vehicle is travelling, as you can see, quite slowly, 3, 4, 5 miles an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is depicted in the image right there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a house which I believe is still occupied by former Bosnian Croat residents of the village. I hadn't spoken to anybody in that home to confirm that. The point where the video is taken from the Landrover from the centre of the village going up, we are now in the same position but now travelling from the centre of the village where the grocery store is and down towards the main highway. The main highway from this point is some 300-400 metres. Coming into the centre of the picture just on the left there is the mosque which had a minaret which was destroyed. To the left there you can see a junction. There's a substantial portion of the village to the left, which you have seen from the aerial shot, but we were unable to go down that with a vehicle at this time. Having left the mosque behind us, we're now approaching the main highway: the main highway is there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's the road between Vitez and Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could travel to Busovaca from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is this the view from the highway looking back into the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Now travelling forward back into the village and you can see the mosque coming into view. That is the school building in Ahmici. Having left the mosque behind us, we're now travelling back to the centre of the village where the grocery store is situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again there appear to be some houses intact there, Mr. Leach. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again it's my information that the intact houses that you see are Bosnian Croat residents of the village and that they were not damaged during the conflict on the morning of 16th April. That is the grocery store that I was mentioning. We travel up a narrow track to a series of intact houses, which are left of centre of the village on the hillside.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that tape number 5 and tape number 6 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No objection. Is that to be their exhibit number, known as tape 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, I wait until the Registrar gives me a number and then he will indicate what they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Dubuisson, will a copy of these be given to the Defence? Will there be duplicates made of cuts?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There can be. There's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Either given to the Defence as all the maps were or put into the record and made available to the Defence so the Defence may ask any questions it wants to, even if it has to re-show these pictures during the cross-examination either at the request of Mr. Hayman or Mr. Nobilo. I think now that we have finished this sequence, unless you have another question concerning the film, this might be a good point to stop, unless you have another question you would like to ask in order to end these two exhibits which were filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No. It is a good time to stop, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We will suspend the hearing. I remind you that we will meet on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday from 10.00-1.00 and I ask the Prosecutor that there be no interruption of the witnesses even if a witness has to come back at a later time to finish his testimony and to be subjected to

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: on you to do this, Mr. Prosecutor. We are now suspending the hearing. The hearing will start again at 10 o'clock on Monday. (12.55 pm)
